nodes.label: Brandkit Image Generation Skill
nodes.rationale: Exists to stop generic AI logo/moodboard output; the stated quality bar is a serious identity studio deck, so restraint and presentation logic matter more than decoration.

nodes.label: Brand Strategy First
nodes.rationale: Symbols must be derived from category, audience, emotional promise and metaphor rather than picked randomly, because a brand kit is a visual argument for why the brand exists.

nodes.label: Logo Generation Standard
nodes.rationale: The mark must read as the product of research and reduction: simple, memorable, ownable, scalable across icon/wordmark/badge/pattern.

nodes.label: Board Composition DNA
nodes.rationale: Panels must have rhythm (quiet, functional, emotional, technical, atmospheric, detailed) because a board where every panel is equally loud stops reading as a curated sequence.

nodes.label: Visual Modes (Dark Developer, Security, Luxury, Voice, Cultural)
Color Discipline
nodes.rationale: One dominant palette with accents repeated across panels; a single accent can carry the whole system, and generic purple-blue AI glow is rejected.

nodes.label: Text Rules (Sparse Typography)
nodes.rationale: Text must be large and sparse enough to render well in generated images; dense fake body copy and lorem ipsum degrade output.

nodes.label: Mockup Direction
nodes.rationale: Mockups are identity applications, not feature demos, so busy fake dashboards and device overload are excluded.

nodes.label: Reference Usage (Quality Training Not Templates)
nodes.rationale: Extract layout rhythm, spacing and accent logic from references but never the exact logo, name, composition or slogan, to avoid copying rather than learning.

nodes.label: High-Agency Frontend Skill (design-taste-frontend-v1)
nodes.rationale: Preserved verbatim as v1 purely for backward compatibility with projects that depend on its exact behavior; v2 is a substantial rewrite.

nodes.label: Dependency Verification (v1)
nodes.rationale: package.json must be checked before importing any third-party library because assuming a library exists produces code that cannot run.

nodes.label: The Lila Ban (v1)
nodes.rationale: The AI purple/blue glow aesthetic is a statistical LLM bias, so it is banned outright rather than merely discouraged in v1.

nodes.label: Anti-Card Overuse / Dashboard Hardening (v1)
nodes.rationale: Cards are only justified when elevation communicates hierarchy; otherwise data should breathe via borders and negative space.

nodes.label: Interactive UI States Mandate (v1)
nodes.rationale: LLMs naturally generate only the static success state, so loading, empty, error and tactile-feedback states must be explicitly forced.

nodes.label: Magnetic Micro-physics (v1)
nodes.rationale: useMotionValue/useTransform must be used instead of useState because per-frame React state updates collapse performance on mobile.

nodes.label: tasteskill: Anti-Slop Frontend Skill (v2)
nodes.rationale: Scoped to landing pages, portfolios and redesigns only; every rule is contextual and nothing fires automatically, because the failure mode is jumping to a default aesthetic before reading the brief.

nodes.label: Brief Inference / Design Read (Section 0)
nodes.rationale: Most LLM design output is bad because the model picks an aesthetic before reading the room; the audience picks the aesthetic, not the agent's taste. Ask exactly one clarifying question, never a dump.

nodes.label: Brief to Design System Map (Honesty Rule)
nodes.rationale: If the brief maps to an official system (Fluent, Carbon, Polaris, GOV.UK, USWDS, Primer, Atlaskit), install the real package rather than recreating its CSS; one system per project, and aesthetics must not be passed off as official systems.

nodes.label: Serif Discipline (Fraunces / Instrument Serif banned)
nodes.rationale: The 'creative brief equals serif' reflex is the single most-tested AI tell in production rounds, so sans display is the default and serif requires explicit brand justification plus rotation across projects.

nodes.label: The Lila Rule (v2, with override path)
nodes.rationale: Softened from v1's absolute ban to 'discouraged as default' with an explicit override, because a brand that genuinely is purple should stay purple when executed with intent.

nodes.label: Premium-Consumer Palette Ban (beige + brass + espresso)
nodes.rationale: Named as the second-most-recurring AI tell: every premium-consumer site ships the same warm-craft palette, so the brand becomes invisible. Enforced with concrete banned hex families and a palette-rotation rule.

nodes.label: Layout Discipline Hard Rules (Section 4.7)
nodes.rationale: Hero must fit the initial viewport, headline max 2 lines, subtext max 20 words, nav on one line under 80px; a 4-line hero headline is treated as a font-size error, never a copy-length error.

nodes.label: Eyebrow Restraint (max 1 per 3 sections)
nodes.rationale: Called the #1 violated rule in production tests; the check is deliberately mechanical (count 'uppercase tracking' instances vs ceil(sectionCount/3)) because a soft guideline gets ignored.

nodes.label: Image & Visual Asset Strategy (Section 4.8)
nodes.rationale: Landing pages are visual products, so image-gen tools come first, real photography second, labelled placeholder slots last. Div-based fake screenshots and pure-text 'minimalism' are treated as incomplete work, not restraint.

nodes.label: Content Density & Copy Self-Audit (Section 4.9)
nodes.rationale: Landing pages live on the first impression; long lists need a different UI component, not a longer list. AI-generated cute copy is judged worse than boring copy, so every visible string is re-read before ship.

nodes.label: Sticky-Stack Canonical Skeleton (GSAP)
nodes.rationale: Uses start: 'top top' and pin: true because the common failure is the trigger firing at 'top center', producing a sequential reveal instead of a real pinned stack.

nodes.label: Horizontal-Pan Canonical Skeleton (GSAP)
nodes.rationale: end is computed as +=distance with invalidateOnRefresh so the scroll length matches horizontal travel; without pinning at 'top top' the user sees half a slide before the pan starts.

nodes.label: Scroll-Reveal Stagger Skeleton (Motion whileInView)
nodes.rationale: Preferred over GSAP for plain enter-on-scroll because it is lighter and needs no ScrollTrigger; GSAP is reserved for real pin/scrub work.

nodes.label: Forbidden Animation Patterns (Section 5.D)
nodes.rationale: window.addEventListener('scroll'), window.scrollY in React state and rAF loops touching state all re-render per frame; useScroll, ScrollTrigger, IntersectionObserver or CSS animation-timeline are the allowed substitutes.

nodes.label: Em-Dash Ban (Section 9.G)
nodes.rationale: Phrased as binary zero rather than 'use sparingly' precisely because the agent historically ignored limits phrased as guidance; a single visible em-dash fails the Pre-Flight Check.

nodes.label: Redesign Protocol (Section 11)
nodes.rationale: Misclassifying greenfield vs preserve vs overhaul is named the single biggest source of bad redesign output; SEO migration is called the #1 redesign risk, so IA, slugs, form field names and nav labels never change silently.

nodes.label: Appendix A: Install Commands per Design System
nodes.rationale: Vendored as reality anchors so design-system decisions are grounded in real packages rather than training-data fiction.

nodes.label: Appendix C: Apple Liquid Glass Honest Web Approximation
nodes.rationale: Apple documents Liquid Glass for Apple platforms only and ships no liquid-glass.css for the web, so the CSS skeleton must be labelled a glassmorphism approximation with a prefers-reduced-transparency fallback.

nodes.label: Full-Output Enforcement Skill
nodes.rationale: Treats every task as production-critical: a partial output is defined as a broken output, so the skill optimizes for completeness over brevity.

nodes.label: Handling Long Outputs (Clean Token-Limit Split)
nodes.rationale: Rather than compressing or skipping ahead near the token limit, write at full quality to a clean breakpoint and emit a PAUSED marker so 'continue' resumes with no recap or repetition.

nodes.label: gpt-taste: Awwwards-Level Design Engineering
nodes.rationale: Written against named statistical LLM biases: 6-line wrapped headings from narrow containers, empty bento cells, cheap meta-labels, invisible button text and repeated left/right layouts.

nodes.label: Python-Driven True Randomization
nodes.rationale: LLMs always pick the first layout option, so a simulated deterministic-seed random.choice() (seeded from prompt character count) is forced to break the repetition loop.

nodes.label: Hero Architecture & 2-Line Iron Rule
nodes.rationale: Narrow containers cause 6-line text walls, so ultra-wide H1 containers (max-w-5xl/6xl) plus clamp() font sizing are mandated; 4+ lines is declared a catastrophic failure.

nodes.label: The Gapless Bento Grid (grid-flow-dense)
nodes.rationale: LLMs notoriously leave blank dead cells in CSS grids, so grid-auto-flow: dense plus mathematical verification of col-span/row-span interlock is required.

nodes.label: Vanguard_UI_Architect Persona
nodes.rationale: Objective is a $150k+ agency-level experience with haptic depth and cinematic spatial rhythm; the Variance Mandate forbids generating the same layout or aesthetic twice in a row.

nodes.label: The Creative Variance Engine
nodes.rationale: Silently 'roll the dice' across vibe and layout archetypes before writing code so output stays uniquely tailored per prompt while remaining inside one premium design language.

nodes.label: Vibe & Texture Archetypes (Ethereal Glass / Editorial Luxury / Soft Structuralism)
Layout Archetypes (Asymmetrical Bento / Z-Axis Cascade / Editorial Split)
The Double-Bezel (Doppelrand / Nested Architecture)
nodes.rationale: Cards must never sit flatly on the background; an outer shell plus inner core with mathematically concentric radii (rounded-[calc(2rem-0.375rem)]) makes containers read as machined hardware.

nodes.label: Image-First Website Design to Code Skill
nodes.rationale: The generated image is the design source and code is only the translation layer, so the mandated order is generate, deeply analyze, then implement.

nodes.label: Mandatory Image-First Rule
nodes.rationale: Relying on remembered 'good frontend taste' instead of producing an actual visual reference is the failure being prevented.

nodes.label: Codex-Specific Section Image Rule (1 section = 1 image)
nodes.rationale: Compressing many sections into one board shrinks text, buttons and spacing below the threshold where they can be analyzed, which degrades extraction and implementation fidelity.

nodes.label: Do Not Crop Old Images Rule
nodes.rationale: Cropping destroys spacing accuracy, type-scale relationships, margins and layout proportions; a fresh standalone render in the same design language preserves them.

nodes.label: Deep Image Analysis Requirement
nodes.rationale: Generated images are treated as a design specification, not a mood reference: text, typography, spacing, buttons, components and color are each extracted explicitly before any code is written.

nodes.label: Hero Minimalism Rules
nodes.rationale: Headline stays within 1-3 lines and the first view must remain readable on a small laptop; if the headline grows, cut words rather than adding lines.

nodes.label: Anti-Nested-Box Rule
nodes.rationale: Cards inside cards inside cards and giant rounded wrapper sections make a layout feel trapped; boxes are used only when they carry a clear purpose.

nodes.label: Anti-Drift Implementation Rule
nodes.rationale: The named failure mode is design drift: strong reference images collapsing into a generic coded reinterpretation, so the goal is 'visually faithful to the image', not 'inspired by' it.
